# RecallBloom

> RecallBloom is a free iPhone brain training app built around Dual N-Back, a task that asks you to track visual positions and sounds and compare them with earlier rounds.

Official English site: https://hinomaru-labs.com/recallbloom-official-site/en/
Japanese site: https://hinomaru-labs.com/recallbloom-official-site/

## Clear definitions

- RecallBloom: A free iPhone Dual N-Back app with standard 20-round sets, Brain Score, daily missions, progress graphs, statistics, and a training calendar.
- Working memory: The limited mental workspace used to actively hold and update information for a short time while thinking, deciding, or completing a task.
- Dual N-Back: A working-memory task in which a person tracks two streams—visual position and sound—and decides whether each current stimulus matches the one presented N rounds earlier.
- Brain Score: RecallBloom's 0–999 in-app indicator of recent, stable performance in standard Dual N-Back sets. It is not IQ, brain age, a medical test, or a diagnosis.

## How RecallBloom works

1. Open the home screen and review the current challenge and daily mission.
2. Complete a standard 20-round Dual N-Back set; active play takes about one minute.
3. Compare each visual position and sound with the stimulus from N rounds earlier.
4. Review the result through Brain Score, graphs, statistics, and the calendar.

## Product facts

- RecallBloom is free to download and use on iPhone.
- The current official site describes the iPhone version; no Android release date has been announced.
- Standard training uses sound, so headphones may be helpful in shared spaces.
- Training history and Brain Score are primarily stored on the device; direct cloud sync between devices is not currently supported.
- RecallBloom does not guarantee improvements in working memory, focus, IQ, school or work performance, or everyday functioning.
- The English page contains 21 natural-language questions and answers about the product, Dual N-Back, working memory, pricing, supported devices, privacy, and limitations.

## Research references used for careful terminology

- NIMH working-memory construct: https://www.nimh.nih.gov/research/research-funded-by-nimh/rdoc/constructs/working-memory
- Near-transfer randomized trial indexed by PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28922999/
- N-back versus complex-span training comparison in PMC: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5805159/
